transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, yeah, thank you. Um, well, it’s kind of a lot, to be honest. I’m a computer systems analyst, and I’ve been doing IT work for a long time. I actually only have a high school diploma, which, you know, I always felt like I had to work twice as hard to prove myself because of that. And I did, I really did, I worked my way up and got all this experience. But lately... I don't know, I just came in because I keep beating myself up constantly. 

It’s like this broken record in my head telling me that I’m not really senior material. I look at the projects I’m assigned to, the system migrations and all the expectations my team has for me, and I just feel this overwhelming sense that I’ve completely fooled everyone into thinking I could handle more than I actually can. I sit at my desk and just feel so guilty, like I tricked my managers into trusting me. I go over and over every meeting, every email, just thinking about how I’m a fraud and how I have no business being in this role. It’s just this heavy, constant guilt that I’m letting everyone down and that they're all going to figure out I'm in way over my head. I just can't shake the feeling that I don't deserve to be where I am, and it's really starting to wear me down, just constantly feeling like I'm a fake.
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like headaches or stomach issues along with these feelings of guilt and self-doubt?

Physical symptoms? Um, no, not really. I mean, you'd think I would, right? With all this stress and constantly worrying about being exposed as a fraud at work. Like, I sit there at my desk, staring at my dual monitors, going over the server logs or whatever, and my mind is just racing with all these negative thoughts. But physically? No, my stomach is actually fine. 

I don't really get headaches either, which is honestly kind of surprising because I stare at screens for, like, ten to twelve hours a day sometimes, especially when we're doing a big system migration. I always make sure to keep a big water bottle at my desk and stay hydrated, so maybe that helps keep the headaches away, I don't know. But yeah, no stomach issues either. I eat pretty normally, mostly just grabbing a turkey sandwich from the deli downstairs on my lunch break. 

It's really just the mental part that's exhausting me. It's all in my head, just this relentless loop of telling myself I don't belong there. I almost wish I did just have a stomach bug or a migraine, you know? Because then I could just take something for it, or tell my manager I need to go home sick and actually have a valid excuse. But you can't really call in sick just because you feel like a total impostor who tricked his way into a senior analyst role. So I just sit there feeling incredibly guilty and inadequate all day, even though physically, yeah, my body is holding up perfectly fine. It's just the guilt that's so heavy.
Are these feelings of being a fraud and guilt usually triggered by something specific happening at work, or are they more of a constant presence for you?

Well, you know, it’s funny you ask that, because I’ve spent a lot of time trying to figure that out myself. I keep trying to trace it back to one specific project, like maybe it was the cloud migration we did back in the spring, or maybe it was a particular code review where someone pointed out a mistake I made. But honestly, when I really sit down and think about it—when I look back over my calendar and my emails and try to pinpoint a trigger—it’s not really tied to any one event. It’s just... there. 

Like, looking back, these really low, heavy, guilty periods have been hanging around off and on for about eleven months now. Almost a full year of just this constant undercurrent of feeling like a fake. And it’s not like it only happens when my boss schedules a one-on-one, or when a server goes down. It’s there when I’m just doing routine maintenance, you know? It’s there when I’m just writing documentation, which is the easiest part of my job. I’ll just be typing up a standard operating procedure, something I’ve done a hundred times, and that voice is just whispering, *They’re going to read this and realize you don’t know what you’re talking about.* 

So, yeah, it’s not a reaction to something going wrong at work. It’s just this persistent, lingering thing that’s been shadowing me for almost eleven months. I wake up with it, I take it on the train with me, I sit with it at my desk, and I bring it home. It’s just always kind of humming in the background, no matter what I’m actually working on.
Have these feelings of being a fraud and guilt affected your relationships with friends or family?

Well, yeah, it definitely has. I mean, it's hard for it not to, right? When you're carrying around this... this massive weight of feeling like you're just pretending to be a competent adult, it kind of spills over into everything. 

I’m still making it to work every day, somehow. I haven't missed a shift, but I find myself just agonizing over every little thing I do. I have to double-check, triple-check my work, even the basic stuff, because I just don't trust myself anymore. I'll write a simple script to automate a backup, something I could do in my sleep five years ago, and I'll sit there running it in a test environment over and over because I'm terrified I've messed it up and it's going to wipe a production database. It takes me twice as long to get anything done because I'm so paralyzed by this idea that I'm incompetent. 

And as for my personal life... yeah, it's taken a hit. I’ve really pulled back from my friends and family lately. My sister called me last weekend to see if I wanted to come over for a barbecue, just a casual thing, and I made up some excuse about being on-call for an emergency patch. But the truth is, I just didn't want to go. I didn't want to sit there and make small talk and have them ask me how work is going, because I feel like if I open my mouth, they're going to see right through me, too. They're going to realize I'm a fraud. 

Plus, my mood is just so unpredictable right now. I don't trust my own judgment. I feel like if I go out, I'll either be a total downer and ruin everyone's good time with my negativity, or I'll try to overcompensate and act like everything is perfectly fine, and that just feels so exhausting and fake. It's easier to just stay home, you know? Just me and the dog. I don't have to pretend around him. But it's lonely. I haven't seen my best buddy, Dave, in probably two months, and we usually get a beer every other Friday. I just keep blowing him off because I don't want to bring him down with all this... this guilt and self-doubt. So, yeah, I guess you could say it's definitely affecting my relationships. I'm just kind of isolating myself because I don't trust myself around anyone right now.
Do you often worry about what other people think of your work or your abilities?

Oh, constantly. I mean... that's exactly it. That's actually the whole reason I finally made the appointment to come in here and talk to someone. I just... I keep beating myself up, day in and day out, over this idea that I’m not really senior material. 

Like, I got this senior analyst title a while back, right? And I only have a high school diploma. I worked my way up from the very bottom, just answering help desk tickets, resetting passwords, crawling under desks to fix printer cables, and somehow I ended up in this high-level spot. But instead of feeling good about it, I just have this overwhelming, sickening sense that I fooled everyone. I really feel like I completely tricked the IT director, the whole management team, everyone... I fooled them all into thinking I could handle way more than I actually can. 

And now I’m just waiting for the other shoe to drop. Every time I send an email, every time I submit a report on system performance or network latency, I’m obsessing over what they’re thinking when they read it. I picture them sitting in their offices, looking at my work, and just realizing, 'Wow, this guy has no idea what he's doing.' It’s exhausting. I'll spend three hours drafting a five-minute update for the morning stand-up meeting because I'm so terrified I'll use the wrong terminology and expose myself as a complete fraud. 

I just keep beating myself up over it, constantly telling myself I don't belong at this level, that I took a job I have no business doing and that I'm letting everyone down by pretending I can do it. Even when I'm driving home, I'll replay conversations I had with the developers, analyzing every word I said, worrying that I sounded stupid. So, yeah, I worry about their opinions non-stop. It's the main reason I'm sitting in this chair right now, honestly, because I just can't take the constant feeling that I'm pulling a fast one on the whole company and that they're all about to figure it out.
Do you feel like a fraud or inadequate in areas of your life outside of work?

Outside of work? I mean... I guess, like I was saying about blowing off Dave and my sister, I definitely feel inadequate as a friend and a brother right now, sure. Because I'm just not showing up for them, and I feel guilty about that. But, honestly, if I really sit down and look at it, it always comes back to the job. That's the center of gravity for all of this. 

My personal life is pretty simple, you know? It's just me and my dog, mostly. There’s not a whole lot to fake there. The dog thinks I'm a genius as long as I remember to fill his bowl. But work... work is where this whole thing just completely consumes me. I know I was just talking about this, but it’s just so huge for me, I can't seem to get past it. It really is the entire reason I finally picked up the phone and came in here to see you. I just... I keep beating myself up, constantly, just hammering away at myself from the minute I wake up to the minute I go to sleep with this idea that I’m not really senior material. 

It’s like a broken record in my head. I look around at these guys in my department with their computer science degrees from big state universities, and here I am, just a guy with a high school diploma who used to crawl under desks to swap out toner cartridges and untangle ethernet cables. And I just can't shake this heavy, sickening feeling that I completely fooled everyone. I fooled the IT director, the HR department, my whole team... I tricked them all into thinking I could handle way more than I actually can. 

And the guilt from that is just overwhelming. I just beat myself up over it every single day, thinking about how I don't belong in that chair and how I'm letting them down by pretending I do. So, yeah, it spills over into my personal life because I'm so exhausted by it, but the core of it—the real heavy guilt—is all tied up in this idea that I'm a massive fraud at the office and I'm just waiting for the day they finally realize it.
Was there a particular event or time in your life when you first started feeling like a fraud?

Well, it's funny you ask that, because I've been trying to pinpoint exactly when this whole... this whole cycle really kicked into high gear. I mean, I've always had a little bit of imposter syndrome, I think most people in tech do, especially when you don't have the formal education to back it up. You're always kind of looking over your shoulder. But this specific feeling? This intense, overwhelming sense that I'm completely faking it and the guilt that comes with it? And the way my mood just keeps swinging around because of it? That's newer. 

If I really trace it back, this noticeable up-and-down pattern really started about a month ago. Yeah, exactly a month ago, actually. It was right after the previous senior analyst, this guy named Mark—brilliant guy, went to MIT, could code circles around anyone—he left for a startup in Silicon Valley. And the director called me into his office, and I thought I was in trouble, honestly. I thought I'd messed up a server migration or something. But instead, he asked me to step up and cover the senior analyst duties until they could find a replacement. 

And at first, I was like, 'Wow, okay, they trust me.' But almost immediately, within days of taking on that workload, that's when the bottom fell out. That's when I started looking at the network architecture diagrams and the high-level strategy documents Mark left behind and thinking, 'I have no idea what I'm looking at.' I mean, I do, technically, but I convinced myself I didn't. And that's when the guilt started, this idea that I had somehow tricked the director into thinking I was capable of filling Mark's shoes. So, yeah, it was about a month ago, right when I got handed those senior duties, that this whole rollercoaster really took off and I started feeling like the biggest fraud in the building.
Are these feelings of guilt and inadequacy interfering with your ability to enjoy your daily activities or perform tasks outside of work?

Well, yeah, I mean... I am still making it to work every day. I haven't missed a shift or called in sick or anything like that. I still get up, feed the dog, get in the car, and go to the office. But once I'm actually there, it's like wading through wet cement because I have to double-check every single thing I do. I mean, I was talking earlier about obsessing over those emails, right? But it's not just emails. If I'm running a basic diagnostic on a server, I'll run it three, maybe four times just to make sure I didn't misread the output. I'll check my command lines over and over before I hit enter. I just don't trust myself at all. It's exhausting just trying to get through a normal Tuesday because I'm so paranoid I'm going to break something and finally prove to them all that I'm an idiot. 

And then, as far as outside of work... enjoying things? That's pretty much gone out the window entirely. Like I mentioned earlier with my buddy Dave, and my sister... I've just completely pulled back from them. I've basically ghosted everyone in my personal life. I let their calls go to voicemail, I leave their texts on read for days. 

And it's not because I don't care about them, it's just... I really don't trust my own mood right now, or my judgment, to be honest. I don't know how I'm going to act or what I'm going to say. I'm so bogged down by this heavy guilt and this constant anxiety that I can barely hold a normal conversation. I just feel like a total wet blanket. I don't want to drag Dave down when he just wants to grab a beer and watch the game, you know? I'd just be sitting there staring at the wall, completely in my own head, obsessing over some network latency report I left on my desk. So it's easier to just stay home. I just don't trust myself to be a normal, functioning person around the people I care about right now, so I avoid it altogether. It feels like my whole life has just shrunk down to going to the office, triple-checking everything so I don't get exposed, and then coming home and hiding out because my mood is just too messed up to inflict on anyone else.
Are you finding it harder to concentrate or make decisions at work because of these feelings of guilt and inadequacy?

Concentrate? No, I wouldn't really say that. I mean, if anything, my concentration is almost... well, it's almost too intense right now. Like, I can sit there and stare at a firewall configuration or a block of server logs for, I don't know, two hours straight without even blinking. It’s not like my mind is wandering off or getting foggy or I’m getting distracted by, you know, my phone or the news or what I'm going to have for lunch. I am completely locked in. I'm focused. It's just that I'm hyper-focused on finding the mistake that I'm absolutely convinced I made, because of that whole fraud feeling I was just telling you about. 

So the raw concentration is definitely still there. I mean, I've always had to have good focus. Back when I was just the guy crawling under desks running Cat6 cables, if you lose focus for a second you plug the wrong thing into the wrong port and bring down an entire department's network. So I know how to lock in. 

And as far as making decisions... no, I'm still making them. I have to, right? In IT, when a switch goes offline or a server crashes, you can't just sit there and twiddle your thumbs. You have to make a call to reroute the traffic or patch the system. So I make the decision. It's not like I freeze up and can't pick an option. I know the protocols. It's just that after I make the decision, that's when the guilt and the second-guessing hit me like a ton of bricks, which is why I end up checking my work four times like I said before. But the actual ability to decide in the moment, or to concentrate on the screen in front of me? No, I haven't noticed any problem with that at all. I'm still doing the actual mechanics of the job just fine, it's just the mental gymnastics afterward that are wearing me out.
Do you find yourself engaging in all-or-nothing thinking, where you believe you're either completely competent or a total failure, with no middle ground?

All-or-nothing... like, black and white? Hmm. No, I wouldn't really say that. 

I mean, it's kind of ironic, right? Because in computers, everything is literal binary. Ones and zeros. A server is either up or it's down, the ping responds or it times out. But with my own head, and how I view my skills? No, I definitely see the gray area. I know I'm not a total failure. I mean, I didn't go to college, sure, but I've been in the trenches of IT for over twenty years. I started out taking help desk tickets, literally just telling people to reboot their machines and resetting passwords, and I worked my way up. So I know I have actual, tangible skills. I know I'm competent at the baseline stuff. If you need a subnet configured or a firewall rule updated, I can do it in my sleep. 

I don't think I'm completely incompetent across the board. I don't walk around thinking I'm useless. The issue is really just this specific senior analyst role. It's like, I know exactly where my middle ground is, and I know I'm standing way past it right now. So it's not that I think I'm a total zero, it's just that I know I'm maybe a... a six out of ten, and the director thinks I'm a nine. And that gap, that space between the six and the nine, that's where all this guilt is living. That's where the imposter feeling comes from. 

So I guess, to answer your question, no, I don't have that all-or-nothing thing going on. I'm actually painfully aware of the middle ground. I just feel like I'm tricking people about exactly where I sit on it, if that makes sense.
Are you feeling like you're able to hide these feelings of guilt and inadequacy from your coworkers, or are they starting to notice a change in you?

Well, I... I really couldn't tell you for sure. I mean, I don't know. 

You have to understand the environment I work in. It's not like we're all sitting around a big conference table pitching marketing ideas and chatting all day. A lot of the time, I've got my noise-canceling headphones on, I'm staring at two, sometimes three monitors, and the only communication I have with the guy sitting in the cubicle literally three feet away from me is through Microsoft Teams. We just ping each other. So in that sense, it's pretty easy to just put your head down and pretend everything is fine. I just type my status updates, send my reports, and keep my mouth shut. I try to put on the mask, you know? Make the usual dry jokes by the coffee machine, nod when people complain about the end-users, that sort of thing. I try really hard to act like the same old guy they've known for years.

But at the same time... I just don't know if it's working. Because I'm doing all that double and triple checking I was telling you about, right? And sometimes people are waiting on me. Like, there was a moment last Thursday, I think, where one of the junior network admins—this kid who just got his degree from state—he was waiting on me to approve a routine routing change. And I just kept staring at the IP tables. I must have read them five times. I could feel him standing behind my chair, just shifting his weight, waiting for the green light, and I was sweating bullets thinking I was going to miss a conflict and take down the VoIP phones. I finally gave him the thumbs up, and he gave me this look. Or... well, at least, I *think* he gave me a look. Maybe he was just bored, or tired, or thinking about lunch. 

Because I'm so deep in my own head with all this guilt about the promotion, and feeling like I don't deserve to be in this chair, I can't really trust my own perception of how people are reacting to me. I'm second-guessing their reactions just as much as I'm second-guessing my own work. So I might be hiding it perfectly. They might just think I'm being a really thorough senior analyst taking his new responsibilities seriously. Or, I might be walking around with a giant neon sign over my head that says "Imposter," and they're all just too polite to say anything to my face. I just... I really have no idea what they're actually seeing.
Do your feelings of guilt and inadequacy stay at the same level all the time, or do they vary from day to day?

It’s... well, it’s pretty much constant, honestly. I mean, maybe it dips a tiny bit on a Saturday if I’m out mowing the lawn or something, completely away from a keyboard, but even then, it’s always running in the background. Like a runaway process just eating up all your CPU, you know? It doesn't really go away. 

In fact, that constant weight... that's literally why I finally made the appointment and came in to see you in the first place. I just couldn't take the noise in my own head anymore. I just keep beating myself up, relentlessly, over the fact that I’m not really senior material. They gave me this title, "Senior Systems Analyst," and it looks great on the email signature, sure, but every time I send a message, I look at that word "Senior" and my stomach just ties itself into knots. I sit there and I just beat myself up because I know, deep down, that I fooled everyone. I somehow managed to fool the IT director, the HR rep, the whole interview panel... I tricked them into thinking I could handle way more than I actually can. 

And now I’m sitting in this chair, and the expectations are way up here, and my actual ability—like I said before, the fact that I don't have the theoretical computer science background these other guys have—is way down there. So, yeah, it doesn't really vary much from day to day. I wake up thinking about how I'm in over my head, I drive to work waiting for the other shoe to drop, and I drive home beating myself up for not just staying in my old position where I actually knew what I was doing. It’s just this endless, exhausting loop of feeling like I conned my way into a job I don't deserve.
Have you been having any trouble sleeping due to these feelings of guilt and inadequacy?

Yeah, sleep is... well, it’s basically become a whole other job at this point. I mean, I used to be the kind of guy who could just shut down, you know? Hit the pillow, out cold, wake up when the alarm goes off. But lately, with all this stuff running through my head... it’s just a mess. 

What happens now is, I’ll either wake up way, way too early—like, my eyes will just snap open at 3:30 or 4:00 in the morning. And instantly, before I even really know what day it is, my brain is already pulling up all these open client tickets. I’ll just lie there in the dark, staring at the ceiling, stressing over whether I misconfigured a VLAN or if I forgot to update a critical security patch for the HR department, or if that junior admin is going to mess up the routing tables because I didn't explain it right. And once that train leaves the station, that’s it. I absolutely cannot get back to sleep. I just toss and turn for hours, watching the clock change, knowing I have to go in and face the music. 

But then, even on the nights where that doesn't happen... like, let's say I actually manage to stay asleep for a solid seven or eight hours. You'd think that would be the fix, right? You'd think I'd wake up refreshed and ready to go. But I don't. I can sleep enough hours and still wake up feeling completely worn out. It’s like my brain is just running heavy background processes all night long, stressing about the job and feeling like a fraud even when I'm completely unconscious. I don't get any actual rest. So either way, whether I'm up at 3 AM staring at the wall or technically sleeping through the night, I just drag myself out of bed feeling totally exhausted before the workday even starts. It's just draining.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or eating habits since you started feeling this way?

Yeah, food is... well, eating just feels like another chore right now, to be honest with you. Normally, I’m a pretty steady eater. You know, I'd grab a turkey sandwich at the deli down the street from the office for lunch, and then come home and make something decent, or at least heat up a frozen dinner if I was too wiped out. But lately, since all this started, my appetite has just been completely off. 

I'll get home from work, and my brain is still spinning from all that stuff I was just telling you about—all the anxiety about the tickets and the junior admins and feeling like a fraud—and I just look at the fridge and think, "What's the point?" The thought of actually figuring out what to make, cooking it, and sitting down to eat it... it just seems exhausting. I don't even feel hungry. So a lot of the time, I end up just skipping supper entirely. Or, I don't know, I might just wander into the kitchen and grab a few bites of whatever is sitting out, like a handful of crackers or a slice of cheese, and that's it. That's my whole dinner for the night. 

And I mean, it's definitely starting to show physically. I was getting dressed the other morning, putting on my standard work khakis—the same ones I've worn for the last couple of years—and I went to buckle my belt, and I actually had to pull it tighter and go down a notch. My belt is definitely a little looser now. Which is strange, because it's not like I'm hitting the gym or going on some strict diet or anything like that. I am definitely not trying to lose weight. If anything, sitting at a desk staring at monitors for nine hours a day, you'd think I'd be putting weight on. But because I'm just not eating, because I'm just picking at a few bites here and there instead of having actual meals... the weight is just kind of dropping off on its own. 

You really don't realize how much your stomach is tied to your brain until you spend all day stressing out that you're going to get exposed as an imposter, and then suddenly you can't even stomach the idea of a simple plate of pasta. It’s just one more thing that's completely out of whack right now, you know?
Are you taking care of your personal hygiene and grooming as you normally would?

Well, yeah, I mean... I think so? I'm still showering and shaving and all that. It's not like I'm showing up to the office looking like I slept in my car or anything. I mean, in IT, the bar for personal grooming isn't exactly sky-high to begin with, right? You've got guys who wear the same wrinkled Star Wars t-shirt three days in a row, but since I got bumped up to Senior Analyst, I've really tried to maintain a certain standard. Khakis, a collared shirt, you know, trying to look the part even if I feel like a total fraud underneath it all. 

So, yeah, I still get up, I take my shower. I might stand in there for an extra ten minutes just letting the hot water hit my back because I'm so exhausted from not sleeping, like I was telling you about, and dreading having to go in and face the servers, but I do get it done. I brush my teeth, use the mouthwash, put on deodorant. I'm not skipping any of the basics. I still get my hair cut every four weeks at the place next to the grocery store. I haven't let myself go or anything like that. It just... it takes a lot more mental energy to get through that morning routine than it used to. Like, picking out a shirt feels like a major decision when your brain is already running through fifty different ways you might screw up the network topology that day. But outwardly? No, I think I look pretty much the same as I always have. Just, you know, maybe with slightly looser pants and bigger bags under my eyes.
Do you feel like a fraud or inadequate in any areas of your life outside of your job as a senior analyst?

Well, outside of work... I mean, work is really the main thing, you know? It’s the whole reason I even came in here to talk to somebody in the first place. I just... I keep beating myself up over this promotion. Like, constantly. It’s this loop in my head that I’m not really senior material. I mean, I only have a high school diploma, right? I didn't go to some fancy tech institute or get a four-year degree in computer science. I just kind of learned on the job, worked my way up from the help desk, resetting passwords and plugging in monitors, and somehow, I managed to fool everyone into thinking I could handle more than I actually can. 

And now I'm sitting in this senior role, and they expect me to design architecture and lead projects, and I just feel like it’s only a matter of time before they realize they made a huge mistake. Like, any day now, the director is going to pull me into his office and say, "Hey, we looked at your last deployment, and it's a disaster, and we know you don't actually know what you're doing." I just feel so incredibly inadequate there. 

But outside of work? Like, in my personal life? I don't know if it bleeds over quite the same way. I mean, I'm not married, I don't have kids, so it's not like I'm sitting around feeling like a terrible father or a bad husband. My life outside the office is pretty quiet. I have a few buddies I'll play online games with on the weekends, or maybe grab a beer with occasionally, but I don't feel like a fraud with them. They know who I am. We just talk about cars or games or whatever. 

But honestly, the work stuff is so heavy right now, it kind of takes up all the oxygen in the room anyway. Even when I'm at home, trying to relax, trying to watch a movie or play a game, that guilt is just sitting right there on my chest. That feeling that I'm an imposter, that I tricked the management team into giving me this title and the salary bump, and that I'm letting down the junior guys who are supposed to be learning from me because I don't even know what I'm doing myself. It’s just this constant, grinding feeling of worthlessness about my career, and since my career is kind of the biggest thing I have going on... yeah, it pretty much ruins everything else, even if I'm not specifically feeling inadequate about, like, mowing my lawn or whatever. It all just traces back to the job and how I shouldn't be in the position I'm in.
Are you finding it difficult to engage in activities you normally enjoy outside of work and personal relationships due to these feelings of guilt and inadequacy?

Yeah, actually. It's funny you ask that, because I was just looking at my patio this past Saturday and... well, normally, weekends are my time to just decompress, right? I mean, I usually really look forward to grilling. I've got this nice Weber setup out back—charcoal, not gas, because you just don't get the same flavor with gas, you know? It takes more work, but it's worth it. I'd usually go down to the butcher on Friday after work, pick up some decent steaks or maybe some ribs, and spend Saturday afternoon getting the coals just right. But lately? I just look out the sliding glass door at the grill with the cover on it, and I just... I don't even care. The cover has been on it for weeks. The charcoal is probably getting damp out in the shed, but I can't bring myself to go out there and mess with it. 

And it's not just the grilling, either. It's everything I used to do to clear my head. I usually love to go fishing. There's this lake about forty minutes from my place, really quiet, good for bass. I used to pack up the truck at dawn, get out there before anyone else on a Sunday morning... but my tackle box and my rods are just sitting right by the door in the garage. Exactly where I dropped them the last time I went, which feels like a lifetime ago. I just leave the stuff sitting there. 

Same with my music. I've got a pretty solid vinyl collection, spent years tracking down original pressings of classic rock albums, and I have a really nice turntable setup in the living room. Putting on a record, dropping the needle, just sitting back in the recliner with a drink... that used to be my nightly ritual to unwind after staring at screens all day. But now? The dust cover is down. I haven't flipped through the crates in I don't know how long. 

It’s exactly what you said—the guilt and the stress from work just kind of bleed into everything. It’s like all that stuff I used to genuinely look forward to just feels completely pointless now. I just sit there on the couch, staring at the wall or the TV without really watching it, thinking about the server migrations and how I’m probably screwing them all up and how I don't deserve my job.
